output.brief: The Android login drop is almost certainly caused by a new vendor rule, not by release 6.14. Corvane's 3 March rule-pack update added a rule that blocks any request from the nettle-http library on the password-login path when it has no edge session cookie. The Android app uses that library for every API call. Blocks began at 10:41 UTC, three minutes after the rule activated. They hit about 41,300 installs, 92% of which had logged in successfully before, so these are mostly real customers. Every Android version failed at the same moment, including old versions that didn't get 6.14. Quick-unlock, iOS and web were untouched. The failures are all HTTP 403 on password submissions, so credential-stuffing, the OS patch, the new password screen and the auth-token change don't explain them. Next step: ask Corvane to switch only that rule to log-only on the mobile password path, keeping rate limits, lockout and other rules on, then confirm in telemetry that Android password success returns to about 96%. Don't roll back 6.14, raise bot sensitivity, or drop blocked attempts from the KPI. Raising sensitivity would block more customers, and the KPI change would hide the problem. My confidence is high. The remaining gap is whether 6.14 has any smaller separate issue.
